fact_sun: The Sun holds about 99.86% of all the mass in the Solar System. Its light takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
fact_mercury: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. From one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days, two of its years.
fact_venus: Venus is the hottest planet because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat. It spins backwards, and its day is longer than its year.
fact_earth: Earth is the only world known to have liquid water on its surface and life. About 71% of its surface is covered by oceans.
fact_mars: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System at about 22 km. Its red colour comes from iron oxide dust.
fact_jupiter: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.
fact_saturn: Saturn is less dense than water. Its bright rings are made mostly of ice and are hundreds of thousands of kilometres wide but very thin.
fact_uranus: Uranus is tipped over by about 98°, so it rolls around the Sun on its side. Each pole gets 42 years of sunlight and then 42 years of darkness.
fact_neptune: Neptune has the fastest winds in the Solar System, over 2,000 km/h. It was found in 1846 by mathematical prediction before anyone saw it.
fact_moon: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth. It is slowly moving away from us, by about 3.8 cm every year.
